# Kyoto Budget Trip Snapshot: 4 Days, Moderate Pace

A public-transit-only plan for 2 adults, built around your **USD 450 on-the-ground budget** and your requested day themes: temples, food markets, nature, and a rainy-day backup. I’m assuming **mid-range local transit, casual meals, and mostly free/low-cost sights**.

# 4-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Spend Plan

## Suggested Stay Areas for Easy Transit
- **Kyoto Station area**: best for budget hotels, JR access, and simple airport/Osaka connections.
- **Gojo / Karasuma**: central, good subway access, often better value than Gion.
- **Shijo / Kawaramachi**: best for dining and buses, but can cost a bit more.
- **Near Sanjo**: convenient for walking, river access, and easy train links.

## Day-by-Day Plan
Day 1: **Arrival + East Kyoto Temples**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, light lunch near Kyoto Station or Gojo.
- Afternoon: Visit **Kiyomizu-dera** and walk the preserved lanes around **Sannenzaka / Ninenzaka**.
- Evening: Sunset stroll in **Gion** and a simple dinner near Shijo.
- Food: Budget set meal or udon/soba.
- Transit: Bus + walking; keep the day compact to avoid taxi use.

Day 2: **Food Markets + Central Kyoto**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Morning: Start at **Nishiki Market** for snacks, tamagoyaki, pickles, tofu, and sweets.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning: Start at **Nishiki Market** for snacks, tamagoyaki, pickles, tofu, and sweets, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Walk to **Teramachi / Shinkyogoku** shopping arcades and stop at **Nijo Castle exterior** or nearby gardens if energy is good.
- Evening: Casual izakaya-style dinner or curry rice near your stay.
- Food: Share small plates so you can sample more without overspending.
- Transit: Subway + walking.

Day 3: **Nature Day in Arashiyama**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Take the train to **Arashiyama** and walk the **Bamboo Grove** early.
- Afternoon: Cross **Togetsukyo Bridge**, choose a riverside walk, and add **Iwatayama Monkey Park** only if you want a moderate climb.
- Evening: Return before rush hour and keep dinner simple near Kyoto Station.
- Food: Bento, soba, or a casual café lunch.
- Transit: JR or Hankyu/Keifuku lines depending on where you stay.

Day 4: **Rain Backup Day**
- Morning: **Kyoto Railway Museum** or **Kyoto International Manga Museum**.
- Afternoon: **Kyoto National Museum** or indoor shopping around Kyoto Station.
- Evening: Onsen-style bathhouse, department store food floor, or a relaxed final dinner.
- Food: Use the day for cheaper indoor meals and convenience-store snacks if needed.
- Transit: Mostly subway/JR plus short walks.

## Budget Breakdown for 2 Adults
| Category | Daily Target | 4-Day Total | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Transit | USD 12–18 | USD 50–70 | Subway, JR local, buses, IC card top-ups |
| Food | USD 40–55 | USD 160–220 | Mix of market snacks, lunch sets, casual dinners |
| Attractions | USD 15–25 | USD 60–90 | Temples, museum entries, optional paid sites |
| Drinks/Snacks | USD 5–10 | USD 20–40 | Tea, coffee, convenience-store items |
| Buffer | USD 10–20 | USD 40–60 | Rain changes, extra transit, small extras |
| Total | USD 82–128 | **USD 330–480** | Keep to the lower-middle range to stay under budget |

## Spending Target by Day
- **Day 1:** USD 80–110
- **Day 2:** USD 75–105
- **Day 3:** USD 85–120
- **Day 4:** USD 70–100

## Best Budget Strategy
- Stay near **Kyoto Station** or **Gojo/Karasuma** to reduce transit time and bus dependence.
- Use **one major paid attraction per day** and fill the rest with free walking areas.
- Eat **one market lunch + one casual dinner** daily instead of multiple sit-down meals.
- Prioritize **train/subway over taxis**; Kyoto buses can be slower and more crowded.
- Keep the rainy-day plan fully indoor so you do not lose value if weather changes.
